evidence: Ov. Met. 10.670: moram celerī cessātaque tempora cursū (Lewis & Short s.v. corrigō)
terms.comment: Literally “to set right the time that was idle”: in Ovid a runner makes up her delay by speed. A poet's phrase, which Traupman gives for everyday use; prose finds no set phrase for it.

sources: Lewis & Short: corrigo · Lewis & Short: cesso
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 89, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
